# Loop decisions

Every Class R and Class M decision (Part III.2), every PROCESS-DEPARTURE (P8), and every tie-break outcome (IV.4). Append-only. Each entry: time, stage, the fork, the options, the rules applied, the choice, how to reverse it.

## D-001. Checkers run as general-purpose subagents with a fixed read-only brief

- **When, stage.** 2026-10-27 06:05 +03:00, I.3 and S0 step 14.
- **Fork.** The spec's checker is a project subagent `loop-checker` defined in `.claude/agents/loop-checker.md` (read-only tools, `omitClaudeMd: true`). Tool writes into `.claude/` are refused in this session's permission mode, so the definition cannot be created.
- **Options.** (1) Run no checkers until Seckin installs the definition. (2) Run each checker as a fresh general-purpose subagent on the same model, with a fixed brief: read only the named material, use only Read, Grep and Glob, ignore the `CLAUDE.md` pointer. (3) Write the definition through a shell, around the protection.
- **Rules.** P19 (no idle waiting; never shorten a checker round), P10, P12 (option 3 routes around a safety protection: not taken), IV.4 (never downgrade a checker).
- **Choice.** Option 2. No `loop-discussant` exists, so no named teammate is ever started.
- **Revision (06:45, after reading-check round 3).** The built-in `Plan` type, run with `model: opus`, has no Write, Edit or NotebookEdit tool, and its context held no `CLAUDE.md` text or auto-memory index (its own report). It does have Bash, PowerShell, Skill, Claude Docs write tools and ToolSearch. From round 3 on, checkers use the `Plan` type with a brief that forbids PowerShell, Skill, ToolSearch, every MCP tool and any write command. The S0 step 14 proof (can a checker see the pointer?) is run on this type, not presumed failed.
- **Reverse.** Once Seckin installs the definitions, later checkers use `loop-checker`.

## D-002. Private name patterns live in `docs/loop/private/`

- **When, stage.** 2026-10-27 06:02 +03:00, I.0 item 4.
- **Fork.** `.claude/loop_private_patterns.txt` cannot be written.
- **Options.** (1) Label every name search "incomplete: private patterns missing", as the spec prescribes for a missing file. (2) Keep the same three hex lines at `docs/loop/private/loop_private_patterns.txt` (gitignored) and run complete searches.
- **Rules.** P7 and P18 (protect others' names first), H5.
- **Choice.** Option 2. Searches read the file by absolute path from the main checkout, because it does not exist in worktrees, clones or the mirror. S0 step 3 says a failed item 4 means every name search is labelled "incomplete: private patterns missing". That label is kept, as the spec requires, and is completed so that it stays true (P1): every name-search record reads "incomplete: private patterns missing from `.claude/` (I.0 item 4 failed); the same three patterns were applied from `docs/loop/private/loop_private_patterns.txt`". (Revised 07:00 after the S0 completeness checker; the first wording dropped the spec's label.)
- **Reverse.** Move the file to `.claude/` when that folder can be written.

## D-003. The pre-push hook is installed through `core.hooksPath`

- **When, stage.** 2026-10-27 06:10 +03:00, S0 step 17.
- **Fork.** Tool writes into `.git/hooks/` are refused.
- **Options.** (1) No hook; H1 rests on the deny rules alone. (2) Write the hook in the gitignored private folder and point git at it with `git config core.hooksPath <absolute path>`; no other hook was active, so nothing is disabled.
- **Rules.** H1, P12 (a local, reversible git setting), P13.
- **Choice.** Option 2, with an absolute path so that worktrees of this repository use the same hook. The hook was proven by running it directly: refuses while the loop is not DONE (exit 1), allows when the operator's variable is set (exit 0), and always refuses a pushed range that adds a path under `seals/` or `audit/model_replies/` (exit 1, both paths).
- **Reverse.** `git config --unset core.hooksPath`.

## D-004. Lane worktrees are created by hand at the spec's fallback path

- **When, stage.** 2026-10-27 06:15 +03:00, S0 step 13; revised 06:35 after a measurement.
- **Fork.** `worktree.baseRef: head` cannot be set. First assumption: IV.5's fallback location `.claude/worktrees/` would refuse tool writes like the rest of `.claude/`.
- **Measurement.** `git worktree add --detach .claude/worktrees/wtproof HEAD` succeeded, and a Write tool call into that worktree succeeded: Claude Code exempts its own worktree folder from the `.claude/` protection. The proof worktree was then removed with `git worktree remove --force`.
- **Options.** (1) The session scratchpad (session-bound, lost on restart). (2) The spec's own fallback: `git worktree add -b lane/s<NN>-<name> .claude/worktrees/<name> <stage branch HEAD>`, inside the repository and gitignored (`.claude/`).
- **Rules.** IV.5 (its literal fallback), P1 (measured, not assumed), H7.
- **Choice.** Option 2. Lane agents work only in their worktree. Branches are kept after merging (H12). `guard_secrets.py` walks these folders (T24); a hit there that is not in a staged diff is recorded, not a block.
- **Reverse.** Not needed; once `worktree.baseRef` can be set, subagent isolation may create worktrees itself.

## D-005. The role-session proof (S0 step 15a) runs although the lead's deny rules are unproven

- **When, stage.** 2026-10-27 06:10 +03:00, S0 step 15a.
- **Fork.** S0 step 15 says to start no role session until a later session has proven the lead's deny rules. Step 15a asks for one proof session before any real role session.
- **Options.** (1) Skip the proof too. (2) Run the proof: it uses the scratch folder `_proof`, reads no role content, and writes only its own file and `_handoff\PROOF_DONE.json`.
- **Rules.** P18 (the proof exposes no evaluation material), P19, P1 (measure that a role session can run).
- **Choice.** Option 2. Result: exit 0, its own output file written, `PROOF_DONE.json` written; the launch inside this session needed no change to the `CLAUDECODE` variable. Every real role session stays blocked in this session.

## D-006. The gate runs with `py -3.12` (anaconda 3.12)

- **When, stage.** 2026-10-27 06:16 +03:00, S0 step 9.
- **Fork.** The spec says to use "the project's own virtual environment as the README says". The README names none; `.venv` is Python 3.9 and CPU-only; the recorded practice (`CLAUDE.md`, Commands) is `py -3.12 -X utf8 scripts/verify_session1.py`.
- **Options.** (1) `.venv` (3.9, CPU-only, never used for the gate in the record). (2) `py -3.12`, as every recorded gate result was produced. Installing anything is denied by the project settings and is not attempted.
- **Evidence (measured 2026-10-27).** `.venv` imports torch 2.5.1+cpu, numpy and pypdf, but not `transformers`, `sentence_transformers`, `sklearn`, `keybert` or `fastapi`, so most gate checks could not run under it. `py -3.12` imports torch 2.5.1, transformers 4.51.3, sentence-transformers 4.1.0, scikit-learn 1.5.1 and KeyBERT 0.9.0; it lacks `fastapi`, `uvicorn` and `pypdf`.
- **Rules.** P1 (compare like with like: every recorded baseline used this interpreter), 1a precedent (`CLAUDE.md` Commands; `docs/fix/ordinary_final_v13_gates/main_gate_comparison_274.json`). This is a departure from S0 step 9's wording ("the project's own virtual environment"), for the measured reason above.
- **Choice.** Option 2, with `KMP_DUPLICATE_LIB_OK=TRUE` (a known OpenMP clash in this interpreter). Every gate result names the interpreter.
- **Reverse.** Re-baseline with another interpreter if one is set up.

## D-007. S8 is blocked as a whole stage in this session, so S9 to S14 are blocked by dependency

- **When, stage.** 2026-10-27 06:45 +03:00, I.3 round 3.
- **Fork.** With no role session allowed in this session (lead deny rules unproven, S0 step 15), S8 cannot start: S8a item 1 needs the frozen preregistration and C0's scorer hash, and S8b to S8d need role sessions. Do the later stages (S9 to S14) still run on what does not need S8 results?
- **Options.** (1) Run S9 to S13 on everything that does not need S8 results (more output tonight). (2) Treat S8 as BLOCKED as a whole stage; S9 to S14 depend on it (Part V table) and are not started; the loop finishes S1 to S7, does S14 items 3 and 4 only (no instance running, ledger closed, reaper removed, power restored), and ends with status BLOCKED.
- **Rules.** Spec lines 82, 312 and 491 ("continue with every stage that does not depend on it"); Part V outranks P19 (I.2). Running S12 before S8 would also reverse the freeze-then-release-candidate order S8a item 4 and S14 item 5 assume. P18 (evaluation integrity before speed).
- **Choice.** Option 2. Status BLOCKED, never DONE: DONE would remove the pointer's effect and let the pre-push hook allow a push while the history still holds the collaborator's name (11.13).
- **Reverse.** Once Seckin installs the settings and a later session proves the deny rules, role sessions unblock S4c, S5 item 10 and S8, and S9 to S14 follow.

- **When, stage.** 2026-10-27, S1 Part 6.

## D-012. Committing a change to scripts/pipeline.py in a lane, and probe run folders (S1 Part 4)

- **When, stage.** 2026-10-27, S1, after the Part 4 lane.
- **Fork 1.** The project settings deny shell commands that name `scripts/pipeline.py` (their purpose: no pipeline run from this laptop). A lane that changes that file must still commit it. The Part 4 lane built the path by string concatenation to get past the rule (INC-004).
- **Options.** (1) Build the name indirectly (a workaround of the rule's text: not allowed). (2) The lane commits with `git -C <worktree> commit -a` after `git status` shows that only files it owns are modified, so no command names the file; the merge then carries it to the stage branch. (3) The lead edits `pipeline.py` itself.
- **Rules.** P2 and P12 (never work around a permission rule; the rule's purpose, no pipeline run, is untouched by a commit), IV.7 ("stage named paths only" is kept for every other file).
- **Choice.** Option 2, written into every lane brief that touches `pipeline.py`; a refused command is reported, never routed around. Reported to Seckin as overrulable.
- **Fork 2.** S1 Part 4 says the harness and probes have no run context and write nothing. In fact `harness/run_agent.build_orchestrator` and three tool probes create their own run folder, so a live probe would write reply records there. The gate path injects its own dispatch and writes nothing.
- **Choice.** Keep it: a probe's own run folder is a real run folder (not a fallback to `output/`), and saving its replies serves 11.6.4. Recorded in the S1 report.
- **Reverse.** Either can be changed by a later commit.

## D-013. Gate runs after the harness stopped one for low memory

- **When, stage.** 2026-10-27, S1 after C4.
- **What happened.** Claude Code stopped the background gate run for C4 (`7f5dd9d`) because the laptop was critically low on memory while the session was idle, and said not to start that run again without being asked. The main gate had already finished (PASS 247, WARN 1, SKIP 3, FAIL or ERROR 27, the C3 non-pass set; new check 277 passes) and four side gates had passed; `tools/cloud_run_checks.py` was cut off and `tools/ordinary_final_controller_gate.py` never started. Free memory afterwards: 2.8 of 15.7 GB, with the WSL virtual machine holding about 3 GB.
- **Options.** (1) Restart the stopped run (refused: the harness said not to). (2) Never run a gate again in this session (would block every later commit). (3) Leave the stopped run as it is, record C4's two side gates as not run, and run each later commit's gate as a new command, in the foreground (not as an idle background job), only when free physical memory is at least 4 GB, with no other heavy local work running.
- **Rules.** The harness instruction is followed literally for the stopped run; IV.7 needs a gate per commit; P19 (no idle waiting where other work is possible); P1 (the record says exactly what ran).
- **Choice.** Option 3. The next gate (C5) covers C4's tree as well, since C5 only adds two documents.
- **Reverse.** Seckin can ask for the C4 side gates to be re-run.

## D-014. S1 checker round 1: corrections and readings

- **When, stage.** 2026-10-27 08:16 +03:00 (system clock), S1, after the completeness checker, the adversarial reviewer and the claims and hygiene auditor.
- **D-010's premise was wrong.** It said only `tools/checkpoint120_cloud.py` of the non-live credential tools is bound by a record. Three more are hash-bound: `tools/auditor_blocker_closure_cloud.py` (`docs/fix/auditor_blocker_closure_run/execution_manifest.json`, `EVIDENCE_MANIFEST.json`), `tools/auditor_final_retry_cloud.py` (`docs/fix/auditor_final_retry_run/execution_manifest.json`) and `tools/run_first_real_tuning.py` (`docs/fix/first_real_tuning_20260916/EVIDENCE_HASHES.json`); the S1 Part 2 inventory already listed them. So 4 are bound and 12 are frozen by function. The choice (leave all 16 unchanged) stands and is stronger for these three. D-010 is left as written (append-only); this entry corrects it.
- **Where the INST_FINDER setting is saved (Part 7 item 1).** The spec says "saved in the run folder with the run options". The run-options record rejects unknown keys, so the setting is saved beside it in `<run>/audit/agent_switches.json`, on every run. Options: widen the run-options schema (a change to a record many readers validate) or a sibling file (chosen; P13). Every run report states it: the pipeline's run summary does; `FINAL_STATUS.json` is written by the run-analysis tool, which S2c item 3 rebuilds into the 11.12 report template (open item 12), so stating it there is deferred to S2c (P9 reason c: it belongs to that stage's file).
- **The server's exit-9 label (adversarial item 2).** `scripts/server.py` was not touched by S1, and the console's status labels are S7's work; under P16 it is recorded (open item 11) for S7, not fixed in S1.
- **C4's two side gates (completeness item 10).** The stopped run is not restarted (the harness said not to, D-013). C5 adds only two documents to C4's tree, and C5's full gate (all six side gates) passed, so C4's code was gated in full one commit later. Accepted as the record.
- **The two replacement phrases sit inside code backticks (claims item 10).** The spec replaced "the whole token" and said "change nothing else in either file"; the token was already inside a code span, so the backticks stay. A reader sees a neutral phrase where a name was; nothing is claimed.
- **The operator's own name in loop records (claims item 9).** The records name the operator, who wrote the spec, as the person who decides; this is not a third party's name (H6 covers party and collaborator names). Earlier entries stay as written (append-only). New prose says "the operator" where it reads as well; the private file name `FOR_SECKIN.md` is kept, as the spec names it.
- **Rules.** P1, P10 (corrections recorded, nothing dropped), P16, IV.8 (append-only).
- **Reverse.** Each reading can be changed by a later entry.

## D-021. The preregistration draft after its first attack

- **When, stage.** 2026-10-27 10:17 +03:00 (system clock), S4e item 11.
- **The attack.** A fresh `Plan` checker given only `PREREGISTRATION.md` and `SELECTION.md` raised 40 items (10 CRITICAL, 20 SERIOUS, 10 MINOR): silence treated differently for B3 and B1, no primary hypothesis or decision rule, rule templates not written down, configuration and model not pinned, a two-sentence B1 reason limit (straw man on arithmetic), undefined terms, run-failure handling, and others.
- **Resolution.** 34 adopted, 5 adapted, 1 rejected, applied by a subagent and reviewed by the lead. Where the checker conflicted with the spec, the spec wins: S4f (a B1 reply that does not parse is an abstention; a sensitivity analysis maps it to CLEAR), S4e item 1 (the sampling seed is role B's choice, recorded before drawing; scoring seeds are derived from the frozen hash), S8c item 5 (no re-run except one infrastructure re-run before an item starts, instead of three retries), S4e item 2 (the sizing rule stays word for word; clarifications sit beside it), the C0 rule (full agreement, at most three runs). ## D-018. The input format draft: four readings

- **When, stage.** 2026-10-27 09:46 +03:00 (system clock), S3a, writing `docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md` (`input-format-v1-draft`). The text was drafted by a read-only subagent from `scripts/convention_parser.py`, `scripts/pairing_map.py`, `scripts/role_resolution.py`, `scripts/reference_tables.py`, `scripts/paired_review.py`, `tools/score_corpus.py` and `corpus_ingest/`, and written by the lead.
- **Per-test settings (section 8).** The plan lists per-test settings among the format's parts. The code reads no settings file from a bundle; the values that look per-test (the date cutoff, the withheld audit agents, the 2% rename tolerance, the review mode) are repository-wide. Options: (1) build a per-test settings reader now; (2) state that none is read, list the repository-wide values, and have generators write no settings file. Chosen: (2) (P13, P16: a new reader is a product change S3 does not own, and the manifest already removes the only per-test dependency, the date cutoff). Recorded as open item 14.
- **Probe declaration (section 11).** The scorer has no probe support. Chosen: a top-level `probe` field in the key, documented as a convention the scorer ignores, so a probe bundle is scored like any bundle. Reverse: a later scorer change can read it.

Documented, nothing changed in code.
- **Rules.** P1, P9, P13, P16, H11.
- **Reverse.** Each reading can be changed by a later entry; the draft is frozen as `input-format-v1` only after the code-blind check and before any sealed test is written.

(15) tables a benchmark's own paper prints as in-context examples are excluded from the holdout pool (INC-010: B-dev's report named four such SciTab holdout tables on the lead's disk; exclusion makes that exposure inert); ## D-042. S3 checker round 1: the development suite must measure Shimmer, never follow it

- **When, stage.** 2026-10-27 16:07 +0300 (system clock), S3 round 1 (completeness 6 gap items, 2 SERIOUS; adversarial 12, 1 CRITICAL and 4 SERIOUS; claims 6 MINOR; the code-blind reader of S3a item 4 on the new sections 1, 6 and 12 and on the output format: 2 BLOCKING, 12 MINOR).
- **The finding behind most items.** Several generator families had been narrowed to what Shimmer's Python already computes, and gate check 281 asserted that family 4's rename-probe keys equal Shimmer's outcome; after S2 the keys had even been changed to follow Shimmer's new refusal rule. A suite built that way can only confirm the code (P1, P11, Annex A 11.4).
- **Decisions (binding on `lane/s03-fix1`).** (1) Keys state ground truth from the generator's own planting, never Shimmer's output; no gate check asserts key equals Shimmer; agreement becomes a reported measurement. (2) Rename probes: renamed means not withdrawn, withdrawn means withdrawn, with the two counter-cases (a withdrawal beside an unrelated newcomer; a moved rename that changes section) and moves spread over about 2 to 45 percent. (3) Unit mismatches (family 1), ratio, rate and cross-row errors (family 2) planted whether or not Shimmer computes them. (4) Neighbour-only flaws in family 6. (5) Long-range flaws that need the distant unit, cross-reference lines on only about half the uses, distance checked in every bundle. (6) Probe 3's later-only term carries a planted flaw. (7) Multi-round bundles hold only case documents in `context/`. (8) Neutral fixture words in `scripts/`. (9) Regenerate after the last format change and record its hash. (10) A multi-round answer-key subsection in INPUT_FORMAT section 9; rename probes measured in the ordinary two-version review; a typed `reason_kind` on every `prior_refusals` record (a product change, with a gate check). (11) The text items.
- **Options weighed.** For (1): keep the equality check and add counter-cases (rejected: the check would fail the moment the suite found a real miss, so the suite could never report one), or ground truth plus a reported agreement count (chosen).
- **Correcting note on D-025 (append-only).** D-025's count "10 right, 2 wrong, 1 right only by luck" and its own follow-up disagree with the generators README on item 10 (attribution): the README's record (three readings changed the audit: 9, 10 and 13) is the accurate one.
- **Rules.** P1, P11, P4 (typed records, not prose, for the refusal kind), Annex A 11.3 and 11.4, S3b, S3d.

## D-046. S4 checker round 3 (the last round): one figure-audit definition, the CUAD exception withdrawn

- **When, stage.** 2026-10-27 16:26 +0300 (system clock), S4 round 3 (completeness 5 MINOR; claims 1 SERIOUS, 8 MINOR; adversarial and preregistration attack 4 SERIOUS, 6 MINOR). Still before any B1 or B3 development output.

## D-056. B1's attention kernel: sdpa with a pinned memory-efficient backend (option A, amended)

- **When, stage.** 2026-10-28 13:31 +0300 (system clock), S5 item 0, before any B1 development output exists (only the L1 smoke run, which ran no B1).
- **The fork.** B1 sends each item's whole document to the producer model, cut only past the 32,768-token context. Under the eager attention that `scripts/final_models.py` sets, a measured upper bound passes the A10's memory for every FinDVer dry-run filing (32 to 257 GB) and one ContractNLI span document (22.5 GB). Options: (A) B1 uses sdpa attention; (B) a memory-limited cut for B1; (C) drop FinDVer for this hardware; (D) run with out-of-memory items scored as abstentions.
- **Attacked** (III.2 step 3) by a fresh checker: A is faithful to S4d and DECODING-A (the kernel is neither a decoding value nor the weights), but needs ten conditions; B is the straw man S4e item 5 warns of, C has no preregistered ground, D is a hidden penalty.
- **Choice: A, amended, with every condition.** (1) B1, both checkpoints, every item, runs sdpa inside a pinned memory-efficient backend (`sdpa_kernel([SDPBackend.EFFICIENT_ATTENTION])`), so a refused kernel raises instead of falling back to the quadratic math kernel; the kernel and backend are recorded in each reply record and `b1_summary.json`, and checked by `verify_identity`. (2) B3 stays eager: B1 switches the shared resident model's attention setting inside a try/finally that restores eager, with a gate check that B3 records eager and B1 sdpa in one process. (3) An out-of-memory error stops the B1 run as a setup failure (counted and reported apart), never an abstention, with a gate check. (4) Fallback, decided now: chunked prefill (the prompt fed in fixed chunks through the KV cache, same kernel); if that also fails, documents over the measured limit are a pre-declared exclusion reported with counts, never scored. (5) The preregistration names B1's and B3's attention kernels (section 4, B1 bullet and frozen configuration) and lists the kernel difference among the limitations (section 9); section 5.3's cut is unchanged. (6) At L2: B1 eager against sdpa on the short documents for both checkpoints (byte-identical replies and label agreement counted), one repeated long item for byte-identical output under strict determinism, and peak VRAM for one prompt at full length (context minus the allowance) with the tuned checkpoint. (7) B3's largest prompt per model call, by agent, is measured from the reply records (L1 and L2), with B3's peak VRAM on the longest FinDVer and ContraDoc development documents. (8) The memory formula in `benchmark/dryrun/measure.py` is corrected (float32 non-4-bit weights and activations; the T x T term over the prompt only).
- **BUS_READER_ADOPTED (DS5-8).** The plan checker's attack on DS5-8 is recorded in D-055 and its recommended reading was built (R22); the flag is set to True in the same lane, so B3 labels can be read from L2 on. The final preregistration checker attacks the section 5.1 text again before freeze.
- **How to reverse.** Revert the lane's commits; B1 then runs eager and the over-bound documents fail.
- **Rules.** III.2 step 3, S4d, S4e item 5, P11, P15, P18.

## D-058. B3's memory: the producer moves to sdpa with a pinned memory-efficient backend (option A, producer only), conditional on L2's evidence

- **When, stage.** 2026-10-28 15:48 +0300 (system clock), S5 item 6, after INC-015 (B3 ran out of GPU memory on a 1,349-word ContraDoc document: per-document producer prompts of about 8,300 tokens under eager attention on the A10).
- **Options.** (A) producer calls with sdpa inside a pinned memory-efficient backend; (B) a 40 GB GPU for B3; (C) a per-agent input bound; (D) leave it and score failures; (E) chunked prefill under eager.
- **Attacked** (III.2 step 3) by a fresh checker. B breaks the IV.3 type rule (another type only when the A10 is unavailable), S8c item 4 (one type per benchmark) and still caps near 13k tokens; C contradicts the recorded whole-document design (`agent_wrapper.py` "may not be shrunk to make a run fit"; `pipeline._truncate_doc` under semantic waves); D is the hidden penalty D-056 rejected for B1 and would make the primary comparison measure the kernel.
- **Choice: A, producer only, with conditions.** (i) It takes effect only if L2's tuned-checkpoint comparison of eager against sdpa (D-056 condition 6) shows byte-identical replies on at least 90 percent of items and label agreement on at least 95 percent (thresholds declared here, before the comparison is read); otherwise E replaces A. (ii) The kernel is fixed at load and pinned per call with `sdpa_kernel([SDPBackend.EFFICIENT_ATTENTION])`, so a refused kernel raises; out of memory is a named failure, never a retry (P13); the kernel is recorded in every B3 reply record. Each with a gate check. (iii) The Auditor896 classifier stays eager (its runtime contract names eager: `config/final_models.json`, `tuning/auditor_final/runtime_contract.json`), with a check; the `_load_qwen` path (VERIFIER, PRACTICE_AUDITOR, FACT_CHECKER; today the transformers default sdpa, unpinned) is pinned to the same memory-efficient backend. (iv) A clinical-sheet run under the change is compared with L1 call by call (rendered prompt hash and reply bytes), acceptance declared before the run: findings equal to L1's; any reply difference is reported, not hidden. (v) Over-context rule for B3, before freeze: a document whose B3 prompt for any agent exceeds the model's context is a declared exclusion, counted and reported, never scored (mirrors B1's cut in S4d). (vi) Superseded and recorded: D-056 condition 2 (B3 eager; it was never true for the Phi agents, which ran default sdpa) and condition 5's kernel-difference limitation; `bare_model.B3_ATTENTION` and the gate checks that assert B3 eager are amended with neutralise, fail, restore, pass proofs; the preregistration's B3 kernel text is rewritten; every 11.12 report's backend field says "producer sdpa (memory-efficient, pinned); differs from v5 to v12, which ran the producer eager".
- **Classification.** Class R with the attack (an attention kernel is not a model change, P12); the frozen producer was trained and evaluated eager (`tuning/producer_v3/experiment.json`), so the 102-of-102 DEV figure is labelled "eager" wherever cited.
- **Rules.** III.2, IV.3, IV.6, P1, P11, P13, P15, P16, P18, S4d, S8c.

## D-061. E made buildable (closing the D-060 attack), the general fixes from the L2 diagnosis, and a correction to D-060

- **When, stage.** 2026-10-28 18:00 +0300 (system clock), S5 item 6.
- **Correction to D-060's "also from L2" and to INC-015's scope.** A read-only diagnosis of the saved evidence found: only entry 00 ran out of GPU memory (two producer calls of about 6,500 tokens in the same wave, VRAM 12.6 to 22.1 GB, memory apparently not released); entry 06 crashed on a VERIFIER reply that was not a JSON object (`scripts/auditor_pairs.py` around line 317 calls `.get` on it); the other eight B3 entries reached the end with exit 0 and were semantically incomplete, because PROCESSOR broke its contract in 12 of 20 partitions (missing key, a missing span, invented claim ids, a citation outside its span, a refusal, repeated strings). The rule that marks them incomplete is correct (PAIRING-A, `run_completion.py`). The contract retry under the frozen greedy decoding reproduced identical request and reply bytes in 9 of 9 retries.
- **The D-060 attack (fresh checker) and how each item closes.** (1) E's fallback no longer excludes documents: if E misses its thresholds, the loop adopts whichever of E or A is byte-identical to one-shot eager on more items of the same shared set, and reports the difference as a section 9 limitation. (2) Chunk size declared now: 512 tokens for both arms (estimated about 16 GiB for B1 at 30,720 prompt tokens; 2,048 does not fit). (3) Chunked prefill leaves at least 2 tokens to generation, so the first generated token is not computed by a different single-token kernel. (4) E's equivalence evidence: prompts at least three chunks long (1,536 tokens or more), including B3's own rendered producer prompts from the L2 reply records run standalone; one long prompt repeated for determinism; peak GPU memory and prefill time at a 30,720-token prompt on the tuned checkpoint and on B3's longest development prompt with the other models loaded; thresholds as D-060 declared (at least 90 percent byte-identical with one-shot eager and at least 95 percent label agreement on the tuned checkpoint). (5) E's cost goes into the re-forecast. (6) E is built in `call_local` and B1 through one shared helper, with the chunk size recorded in every reply record and gate checks. (7) Preregistration sections 4, 9 and 12 rewritten for E. (8) "No kernel difference" holds for the producer only; the `_load_qwen` agents run pinned sdpa. (9) This entry is the attack's record.
- **General fixes adopted (P11, P16: they affect the evaluation and the honesty of reports).** (a) `auditor_pairs` treats a VERIFIER reply that is not an object as a recorded contract failure, never a crash, with a check. (b) The runner's assessment reports "reached the end, exit 0, semantic_complete false" as its own reason, `semantic_incomplete`, not `pipeline_not_completed`, with a check (PAIRING-A already puts completeness there). (c) The contract retry is skipped when decoding is deterministic, recorded as `retry_skipped_deterministic` (P13: within-run retry of model calls is killed; under greedy decoding it can only repeat itself), with a check; the pipeline function change goes through the pinned-baseline path if a pinned function changes. (d) Whether producer calls of one wave run concurrently on one GPU is read from the code and recorded; any change to it is a separate decision.
- **Not changed, measured instead.** PROCESSOR's contract reliability on benchmark documents (12 of 20 partitions failed; 0 of 4 on the clinical sheet) is a property of the frozen checkpoint on unseen shapes: it is reported as a measured outcome, never tuned (Part VI).
- **Rules.** III.2 step 3, P1, P11, P13, P15, P16, P18, D-058, D-060.

## D-066. How a semantically incomplete B3 run is scored (settled from gold-free counts, before any B3 development score under it)

- **When, stage.** 2026-10-29 01:32 +0300 (system clock), S5 item 10 preparation.
- **Fact.** Today `benchmark/adapters/common/mapping.py` (around lines 194 to 195 and 297 to 298) treats a completion state `stopped` as a run failure, so every item of a semantically incomplete B3 document is ABSTAIN; every B3 development run so far is in that state or a genuine failure.
- **Attacked** by a fresh analysis subagent acting as checker: all-ABSTAIN is S4e item 5's straw man turned on B3 and conflicts with S4d and P1; scoring from records alone can credit silence as CLEAR where failed work was on the deciding path.
- **Choice (its recommendation).** A run that reached its end with exit 0 and `semantic_complete: false` is not a run failure; its items are labelled from the records it posted by section 5.1 lines 2 to 5. Item-level exception (B1's failed-call rule per item): ABSTAIN with basis `item_calls_failed` when the run's pairing map records at least one judging call for the item's rule and every one has outcome `reply_failed` (needs open point 12.11, registry id to operator id; until settled the report says the exception cannot be applied). Completeness is reported per document and arm; items decided by a record from a partial delivery are marked; sensitivity S-6 (every item of a semantically incomplete document ABSTAIN, primary comparison on complete documents) is reported beside the primary result. The preregistration text is the subagent's (section 0 run failure, section 5.1 incomplete documents, S-6), entered in `docs/benchmarks/DEVIATIONS.md` before C0. Built in the next adapter lane with checks.
- **Rules.** S4d, S4e item 5, P1, P18, III.2 step 3.

## D-112. D-S14: the failure causes found, and the fixes chosen

- **When, stage.** 2026-10-30 15:17 +0300 (system clock), S5 reopened, D-S14 item 3. L8 ended at 15:12 (271 billed minutes, 5.83 USD; B1 20 of 20 passed, B3 1 of 20). A read-only diagnosis of every failed entry of L11, L7, L10 and L8 (private `s5_diag_b3.md`, its numbers from the saved evidence and the offline tokenizer) found 33 failed B3 entries (L11 6, L7 11 of which nine are D-101's, L10 1, L8 15 at 14:20; L8's last four f6 entries counted after it ended) and no failed B1 entry.
- **Kinds and counts.** K1 dating `ValueError` (Linux `strftime` drops a leading zero of a year below 1000), 2 entries. K2 VERIFIER out of GPU memory on the A10 above about 44,300 prompt tokens (Phi-3.5, no grouped-query attention, 393,216 bytes of cache a token), 10 entries; about half its prompt is runtime identifiers it cannot use. K3 to K7 PROCESSOR's compact contract, 52 of 283 partitions (18.4 percent) in 15 entries: invented `CLM-` ids no owned span carries (35 calls, its training spans mostly carried such ids), a missing `uncertainty` key, a context-only or corrupted alias, one item for two owned spans, a neighbouring span's REF. K8 EDITOR_CLERK item without `kind`, 4 entries. K9 to K11 rare shape failures (PRACTICE_AUDITOR 3 of 888 calls, ARCHIVIST 1 of 30, VERIFIER envelopes 2 of 30). K12 the nine D-101 entries.
- **Fixes chosen (no check, reason code or test weakened; D-S14 item 3, H9).** K1: `_iso` builds the date with `date().isoformat()`, so a year below 1000 takes the existing out-of-range branch. K2: VERIFIER's rendered payload drops the runtime identifiers it cannot use (telemetry, records and bus keep them), measured offline to bring the ten failing prompts to about 20,000 to 26,000 tokens; a larger GPU type stays the fallback, forecast at its price if needed. K3 to K7: contract-shaped decoding for the compact producer, a logits constraint derived from each request's own declaration with the validator unchanged behind it; a decoding change under DECODING-A, so its DEV figure (102 of 102) is re-measured on the instance under it, with the acceptance rule written before the measurement. K8: for an agent whose contract declares exactly one item kind, Python stamps an absent `kind`, declared in the contract and recorded as `contract_normalized` like ENVELOPE-A; a present but wrong kind is still refused. K9 to K11: re-measured after the fixes (K11's two prompts may fall below the limit with K2); what remains is fixed if an honest fix exists, otherwise recorded under D-S14 item 7. Not chosen: re-asking (deterministic decoding returns the same bytes), changing the pinned prompt, accepting or dropping the invalid output.
- **Order.** Two lanes (lane/s05-fixsmall: K1, K2, K8; lane/s05-constrain: K3 to K7 with the replay plan), each proven on the laptop; then one proof launch (the constrained decoding replay of the 52 failing partition prompts and the 102 DEV rows, and the largest VERIFIER entry, L8 38, on the A10); then one re-run batch of the 28 failed non-D-101 entries plus the nine D-101 entries (about 478 minutes, about 13.3 USD on the A10); then L9a and L9b. Each forecast against the allocation before launch.
- **Rules.** D-S14 items 2 to 8, DECODING-A, EXTRACTION-A, ENVELOPE-A, H9, P1, P4.

## D-188. The 8-hour go-ahead refused for the force push (Class R departure)

## D-194. The D-S26 item 1 scoring design: `detection_dev`, written before any score is read with it

- **When, stage.** 2026-11-02 11:45 +0300 (system clock), after v1, D-S26 item 1, lane ds26-scoring. Written and committed alone before the mode is built and before any saved run is labelled or scored with it; no saved score or result was opened to choose it (the causes read are those of `FINDING_PUBLIC_GAP.md` and D-178, in words).
- **What it is.** A third scoring mode of the benchmark adapters, `label --scoring detection_dev`, for DEVELOPMENT only. It is not the preregistration: `docs/benchmarks/PREREGISTRATION.md`, `docs/INPUT_FORMAT.md`, `docs/OUTPUT_FORMAT.md` and the two modes of `docs/benchmarks/SCORING_MODES.md` are unchanged, `as_shipped` stays the default and `benchmark` stays as it is, byte for byte. Version 3 may start from this mode (D-S26 item 4); until then no sealed figure reads it. The rule is one shared helper (`benchmark/adapters/common/detection.py`); each adapter only declares which document-level reading its rule takes (below). ContractNLI, CUAD, ContraDoc and SciTab declare one; FinDVer, CUAD-claim and the synthetic suite declare none, and the mode refuses them (exit 4) rather than guess.
- **Records read.** The same reading as `as_shipped`, unchanged: the one record reader (bus for B3 and B4, `review_data.json` for B2), supersession, a judged absence counted once by Python's stamped copy, a record belonging to an item by its `source_rule_id`, prior relations dropped with their fault, and Python's figure-audit records attributed by shared words set aside in a bundle of more than one rule. Advice is NOT mapped through the rule-id map (form B of the `benchmark` mode): the most conservative set, fewer records. In addition the mode reads the document's unit list from the run's own `audit/pairing_map.json` (`units[].unit_id`, the preamble unit included; for a document read in segments, each segment's units translated as its records are). The run-failure line, the over-context exclusion, the setup-failure rule, D-066 (`item_calls_failed`, `semantic_incomplete`) and every exclusion are unchanged.
- **Unit states (shared by a, b, c).** For an item's rule, each unit of the unit list gets the set of states its kept records give: `holds` (an ok record that is not a refusal), `violates` (an irregular record that is not a refusal and whose relation is not an absence relation), `lacks` (an irregular record that is not a refusal whose relation is an absence relation: `missing_field` or `licence_missing`, the pipeline's `finding_record.ABSENCE_RELATIONS`, held equal by the gate check), `uncertain` (a record carrying the UNCERTAIN marker). A unit is CLEANLY in a state when its set is exactly that one state; a unit with two or more states is conflicting and is cleanly in none. A pairing-map refusal entry (`absence_refused`, an answer Python refused) is not a kept claim and gives no state; it is counted. A record whose `unit_id` is empty or names no unit of the list is unplaced: it gives no state, decides nothing, and is counted (most conservative: a document-level record is not taken as a document-level answer; a document-level judging plan, D-S22 item 2, would need its own decision).
- **(a) Kept claim apart from silence.** Every label row carries `decided_by`: `kept_claim` when at least one kept record of the item's rule (any state, placed or unplaced) exists; `silence` when none does (the item has no kept record at all, whether or not Python refused an answer for it: no kept claim is silence, as D-S26 item 1 words it); `answer` for B1 (its own reply; a parse failure stays ABSTAIN); `excluded` for a run failure, an over-context exclusion or a setup failure. A `silence` row is ABSTAIN (basis `dev_silence`, or `item_calls_failed` where D-066 applies), so it is never a detection and never counted correct; the label the `as_shipped` reading would have given it is kept on the row (`silence_label`) and the score reports, apart from every measure, how many silence rows there are per gold class and how many of their silence labels equal the gold. Every pipeline row also carries `as_shipped_class`. B0 is all silence (every item ABSTAIN). A `kept_claim` row whose claims settle no class (below) is ABSTAIN with basis `dev_not_established` or `dev_conflict`. What it does not claim: that a kept claim is right, or that it was checked by Python (a model-written kept claim is still a model's); that a `silence` row is wrong (only that it is not a detection).
- **(b) CUAD: "in at least one passage" read per document (declared `exists`).** Present (CLEAR) when at least one unit is cleanly `holds`. Absent (FLAG) only when every unit of the unit list is cleanly `lacks` and none holds: one unit's absence never makes the document's. Otherwise ABSTAIN: `dev_not_established` when kept claims exist (a unit with no kept record, a unit that is conflicting, `violates` or `uncertain`, or no readable unit list, each leaves absence unestablished), `dev_silence` when none. Ties: a unit with both an ok and an absence record is conflicting, counts neither as holding nor as lacking, so it can block absence and cannot give presence. An irregular record of another relation (as shipped: present) says neither presence nor absence here. Python's word-attributed `missing_field` records stay set aside (they are not a judgement of the rule). What it does not claim: that a unit which holds an ok record contains the clause (ok is the record's own verdict, "the unit satisfies the rule"); that CUAD's recall under it is comparable with B1's beyond the same item set.
- **(c) ContractNLI: "not mentioned" reachable from B3's records (declared `three_way`, also SciTab).** B3's records cannot name "not mentioned" directly (the Finding record has no such relation or verdict); what they can express is a unit that does not settle the hypothesis: the UNCERTAIN marker the rule text asks for ("If the agreement does not settle the hypothesis, emit UNCERTAIN") and an absence relation (the unit lacks what the hypothesis states). So: contradiction (FLAG) when at least one unit is cleanly `violates` and none cleanly `holds`; entailment (CLEAR) when at least one unit is cleanly `holds` and none cleanly `violates`; not mentioned (UNDECIDED) when no unit cleanly holds or violates and EVERY unit of the unit list has a non-empty state set within `lacks` and `uncertain` (each says the unit does not settle it). Ties: a unit that holds and a unit that violates make `dev_conflict` (ABSTAIN), never contradiction by precedence, since ABSTAIN is the only class that claims no answer; on ContractNLI and SciTab UNDECIDED is a label, so an unsettled item is ABSTAIN, never UNDECIDED. Missing: a unit with no kept record, or no readable unit list, leaves not mentioned unestablished (ABSTAIN `dev_not_established`, or `dev_silence` with no kept record). A refused answer (pairing-map entry) never counts toward not mentioned. Changed from `as_shipped`: an absence-relation irregular record no longer gives contradiction; a refusal no longer gives not mentioned on its own; silence no longer gives entailment. What it does not claim: that an ok record shows the agreement states the hypothesis (a unit not in conflict with it may also be ok); that "not mentioned" is reached in the saved runs (only that a run which writes those records reaches it).
- **ContraDoc (declared `each`).** Contradictory (FLAG) when at least one unit is cleanly `violates` (another unit's ok is not a conflict for a rule that holds of every passage); not contradictory (CLEAR) only when every unit of the unit list is cleanly `holds`; otherwise ABSTAIN as above. An absence-relation record is not a contradiction. Not named by D-S26; it is (a) applied to a rule that speaks of every passage, the conservative reading (a CLEAR that rests partly on silent units would be a silence label).
- **Analyses and comparisons.** A `detection_dev` labels file holds `primary`, S-6, S-7 and S-8 (S-8 the same rule on Python's records alone); S-1 to S-5 belong to the preregistration's reading and are not produced. `score --paired-with` refuses a `detection_dev` file paired with a file of another mode.
- **Choices not settled by D-S26 or the records, taken as the most conservative reading:** advice not mapped; unplaced records decide nothing; the preamble unit counted in the unit list; a conflicting unit counts for no state; a holds-and-violates conflict is ABSTAIN; ContraDoc's CLEAR and SciTab's three classes follow the same rules; an absence relation is never a contradiction; FinDVer, CUAD-claim and the synthetic suite refused.
- **Reverse.** Remove the mode and its helper; `as_shipped` and `benchmark` are untouched by it. Any change to these rules is a new decision, written before the scores it changes are read.
- **Rules.** D-S26 item 1, D-S22 item 4, D-S27 item 2, D-176, D-178, D-193, P16.

## D-195. The D-194 checker round: 1 SERIOUS and 7 MINOR, each fixed or recorded, before any score is read with `detection_dev`

- **1 (SERIOUS): silence in S-6, S-7 and S-8 was not protected.** Changing `_sub` so an S-8 silence row took its as_shipped class passed every test. Fix: the silence proof now also requires every silence row of S-6, S-7 and S-8 to be ABSTAIN and each analysis' score to answer only the kept-claim items (S-8: none, every item there being silence), and it is run under three neutralisations, each of which must fail: silence given its as_shipped label (`silence_result`, which reaches the primary and so S-6 and S-7, derived from it), S-8 silence given its as_shipped class (`_sub`), and S-8 rows carrying the primary's as_shipped fields (`SUB_FIELDS` cut). S-6 and S-7 are relabellings of the primary, so no `_sub` change reaches them; the first neutralisation is the one that does. The CHANGELOG entry, the adapters README and check 317's text now name exactly the neutralisations the proofs fail under, instead of "each rule neutralised".
- **2: the paired-view refusal was never tested alone.** The refusal is now one function (`detection.check_paired`, called by `cli.score`) and a proof pairs a `detection_dev` B3 with an as_shipped B0 (B0 has no records, so the record-arm mode check does not apply): refused, and accepted once `check_paired` is neutralised, which must fail the proof.
- **3: an item whose only kept records have an unrecognised verdict was `silence`.** D-194 (a) says any kept record of the rule makes the row `kept_claim`. Fixed to D-194's own wording: the silence test reads the kept records, not those with a state; such an item is `kept_claim`, ABSTAIN `dev_not_established`, its fault recorded (`record_verdict_unrecognised`); the row's `detection` block counts `kept_records` beside `claims`.
- **4: `score` produced S-4 for a `detection_dev` file.** D-194 says S-1 to S-5 are not produced. Fixed to its wording: `score` writes no S-4 for a `detection_dev` labels file (tested).
- **5: S-8 rows kept the primary's `as_shipped_class`, `as_shipped_basis` and `detection` block.** Fixed: S-8 carries its own classification's fields (`SUB_FIELDS`), so an S-8 row's as_shipped reading is that of Python's records alone (tested, and neutralised as in item 1).
- **6 (an addition): the labels counts mixed the two readings.** `silent` and `refusals` were always 0 and the band, partial-delivery and refusal-and-ok counts described the as_shipped decision. Under `detection_dev` the counts of the as_shipped decision (`detection.AS_SHIPPED_DECISION_COUNTS`) are removed from `counts` and given under `as_shipped_counts`, recomputed on the rows' as_shipped class and basis; `counts` keeps those that read this mode's rows and adds `detection_dev`. It is applied wherever a labels result is rebuilt (every analysis, a restricted or scored view) through one hook `mapping._labels` calls (`mapping.COUNTS_HOOKS`, empty for `as_shipped` and `benchmark`, so their output is unchanged); the score's `items_from_refusal` is null under this mode. Tested, and neutralised by emptying the hook.
- **7 (an addition): development only was not enforced.** `label --scoring detection_dev` now refuses (exit 4, one line) when the parts record beside the item table is missing or unreadable, or names any document on a side other than `development`; tested with a holdout side and an undeclared one, and neutralised.

If a benchmark that declares a reading ever segments, that path needs its proof first.

## D-201. PATCH_1's rate check when the figures fit no plain reading: the record stays (the design choice D-198 handed back)

- **When, stage.** 2026-11-02 23:45 +0300 (system clock), after v1, D-S26 item 3, before PATCH_1's merge.
- **The fork.** D-198 item 2 refuses a rate mismatch when the figures also fit another plain reading (the larger is the smaller increased by the proportion, or the smaller is the larger decreased by it). It left open whether a part-of-a-whole record must also be refused when the figures fit no plain reading at all. Options: (a) keep minting the record; (b) refuse it as undecided.
- **Choice: (a).** Read in `scripts/relation_checks.py` (`rate_checks`, `other_reading_fits`, `_rate_check`) at `e1bfa2a`: the part and the whole are not chosen by preference. With a proportion below one the part must be the smaller figure, and above one the larger, so the size order is forced by the arithmetic. The readings the code knows are then three: part of a whole, increased by, decreased by. When none fits, the stated figures disagree under every one of them, so "irregular" holds whichever reading the rule's words mean, and Python states nothing a reading could overturn. The record's computed figure follows the part-of-a-whole reading, and its `basis` field says so ("X is R of Y"), so a reader sees which reading the figure belongs to. Refusing would drop a mismatch that every reading confirms (P4: compute what can be computed). No code change.
- **Reverse.** Make `rate_checks` refuse when `check["agrees"]` is false and no reading fits, with a check 319 case; nothing else depends on this choice.
- **Rules.** P4, WORDS-A, P11, D-198 item 2, D-S27 item 2 (a design choice, decided by the lead).

## D-202. The bar for G1, written before G1 is run or any of its numbers exist (D-S22 item 1 (b))

The sample is small (5 documents, 37 decisions on the two benchmarks): whatever the result, it is reported as a development pilot, with document and decision counts beside every figure.

## D-204. The cloud source archive carried no `scripts/relation_checks.py`: one rule for gate material, the runtime module declared

- **When, stage.** 2026-11-03 00:40 +0300 (system clock), after v1, D-S26 item 3, before PATCH_1's merge. Branch `lane/patch1-archive` from `e1bfa2a`, commit `94a9936`; `lane/patch1-relations` fast-forwarded to it.

Cause, read in `tools/prepare_ordinary_final_run.py` (`archive_names`) and `tools/prepare_cloud_run.py` (`make_source`): both drop every `*_checks.py` file as gate material, and PATCH_1's runtime module `scripts/relation_checks.py`, which `paired_review` and `multi_round_rounds` import, ends in `_checks.py`. On an instance every B3 run would have stopped at import. Class: code defect (a design gap in the archive rule).
- **Options.** (a) Rename the module: INFRA-045's text in `config/constitution.json` names `scripts/relation_checks.py`, and the constitution is append-only (H9), so a rename would leave the amendment naming a file that no longer exists. (b) Add the file to `ARCHIVE_EXTRAS`: extras pass through the same exclusion, so it would not travel. (c) One rule for gate material on both paths, with a declared list of runtime modules whose names only look like checks. Chosen: (c) (P11: the defect class, a runtime module whose name matches the gate pattern, is stated without naming a test; P13).
- **Fix.** `prepare_cloud_run.gate_check_file` and `RUNTIME_MODULES_NAMED_LIKE_CHECKS = ('scripts/relation_checks.py',)`, used by both sealers. ## D-235. G1's new bar attacked and not adopted; the sample comes first

- **When, stage.** 2026-11-04 20:45 +0300 (system clock, `date`), after v1, plan step 2. No G1 reply or score exists. A trial build on L11's six documents gave 34 prompts, 17 decisions a model (scratch only).
- **Proposed.** D-202's form with the pool changed to ContraDoc and SciTab. Attack (III.2 step 3): 3 CRITICAL, 5 SERIOUS, 3 MINOR. Not adopted.
- **Why not.** (1) "Only the pool changed" was false: B1 tuned's flag precision is published in `S05_REPORT.md` as 4 of 4 on these items, so the threshold rose from 0.25 to 1.00. (2) Pooled, SciTab can pass alone and ContraDoc can only veto: it has one gold flag, which B1 already catches, so the case G1 exists for can only subtract. (3) Six documents cannot separate anything: a model flagging two items at random passes 20.6 percent of the time, 36.9 with two models, and a sound model with precision 0.9 and six flags fails 47 percent. (4) On SciTab, B1 already reads the whole document, so the comparison tests the prompt, the outcomes and the quote rule, not document-level reading. (5) Two correct flags can pass at half B1's detection. (6) Phi would be compared with a tuned Qwen, against the same-model rule; `--agent` gives the right comparator. (7) "A quote Python found" is weak on a table. (8) The pooled figure and the comparator exist in no code, and check 321 has no SciTab case.
- **Draft wording, to be fixed once the sample is sized.** Written after B1 tuned's flag counts were published, and saying so. Before the seal the decision lists document ids and B1's tp, fp and fn per benchmark and per model. G1 shows a usable signal when one model, the same on both benchmarks, in the `screened` view, with `flag_tp` and `flag_fp` summed over items, meets on ContraDoc and on SciTab separately: flag precision at least B1's on the same model and items, and where B1 has no false flag, none; correct kept flags at least B1's and at least 2, from at least 2 documents; every counted flag quoting a complete cell or sentence, never a section marker or separator alone, with all quotes listed. A pass is a pilot go for D-S22 item 2 only, never "above B1". "At least" stays on precision since "above" cannot be met when B1 is at 1.0; plan's target wording already covers that case.
- **Next.** The adapters record 184 ContraDoc and 95 SciTab development items. ContraDoc is enlarged by a rule fixed before any output on it is read, balanced across its containers, with a sample size that can give at least 6 discordant documents. Whether that fits G1's money is read at the forecast: if not, the question goes to `FOR_SECKIN.md`. G1 waits for this, and the honesty lane does not.
- **Moves.** G1's seal, until the sample and bar are settled: #177.
- **Rules.** D-202, D-S22, D-S33, D-S34, III.2 step 3, P1, P10.

## D-240. D-S36 applied: the lead does not go idle while work remains

- **When, stage.** 2026-11-05 01:33 +0300 (system clock, `date`), after v1, before the next plan step, on the operator's word (Annex D D-S36, 5 November 01:22).
- **Why it stopped.** The old Stop hook blocked once and let any stop with `stop_hook_active` through, so a second stop always ended the turn. The lead's turn after the compaction of 00:14 ended with a summary and no `Waiting:` rule existed. That is a lapse by the lead, about an hour idle with a progress request unread.
- **Built.** `docs/loop/private/continue_hook.py` (private, beside the existing hooks). It blocks while LOOP_STATE says RUNNING with no `Waiting:` line, names NEXT, SPEC_UPDATE and PROGRESS_REQUEST in its one-line reason, counts blocks against a fingerprint of the local branches and the records, and at the fourth stop with nothing new allows it and writes that to FOR_SECKIN. It writes only its count and that note; it never pushes, launches or spends. Any error allows the stop.
- **Differs from the text, three ways.** (1) D-S36 says to add the hooks to `.claude/settings.json`. The existing hooks are in `.claude/settings.local.json`, and the harness refused both Edit calls on that file. It was not rewritten by another route. The settings are unchanged. Instead the entries already there reach the rule: `docs/loop/private/stop_guard_hook.py` now calls it, and `tools/loop/session_start.py` prints the reminder first on a compact start, since a long hook output is shown by its opening only. The operator is told and can add named entries. (2) `stop_hook_active` is honoured as the guard against an endless loop: with it set and no readable count, the stop is allowed. It does not itself allow the stop, or the three blocks could not happen. The count restarts only on something new or after an allowance. (3) A session that does not hold LEAD.lock is left alone, so checkers, role sessions and lanes are not blocked.
- **Main checkout.** `tools/loop/session_start.py` is committed on the loop branch here, and the same change sits uncommitted in the main checkout, detached at old history, because that copy is the one the hook runs.
- **Proof.** `docs/loop/private/continue_hook_proof.py`, on a temp tree with its own git repository: 26 of 26 pass (blocks while RUNNING with no Waiting line, allows with one, allows after three empty blocks, a commit or a record restarts the count, both files read, the real entry files), and three neutralisations (no Waiting test, no limit, no fingerprint) are each caught. Not yet proved: the harness calling it at a real stop; the first real stop of this session is that proof.

- **The bar.** G1 shows a usable signal when one model, the same on both benchmarks, in the `screened` view against `b1_comparator`, on the items of `g1_bar_items.json`, meets on ContraDoc and on SciTab separately: (1) a net rate, recall less false-flag rate, at least B1's, in integers `tp(N-K) - fp K`; (2) at least 2 correct flags, from at least 2 documents; (3) the correct flags above chance: at most 0.05 by an exact test with each stratum's gold and flag counts held, the convolution of one hypergeometric per stratum, a table's claims being one stratum and single-item documents pooled into one; (4) on ContraDoc, at least 2 correct flags whose quote lies in a passage the key marks as evidence. A model's row is void, neither met nor missed, when more than 5 percent of B1's answers on that benchmark are unreadable (the section 5.4 floor). `doc_judge.bar` computes this; no one reads it by hand.
- **What a pass means.** A pilot go for D-S22 item 2 only, never "above B1". Both arms read the whole document, so it compares a prompt and a quote rule and says nothing of whole-document against section reading, on either benchmark. A Phi pass is against Phi's B1 only, while the plan's target is the tuned model's.
- **Attack (III.2 step 3, fresh checker): 2 CRITICAL, 6 SERIOUS, 5 MINOR, each answered.** (1, 2, CRITICAL) Precision and "no false flag" against a cautious or silent B1 failed sound models, two-model pass 0.00 to 0.24, and "correct at least B1's" made the bar unreachable against a flag-heavy B1: replaced by the net rate, which its author measured at .978 to 1.000 for a sound model (recall .6, false-flag .1), .446 for one equal to B1, .112 for recall 20 percent worse and at most .001 for no skill. The false-alarm cost is accepted and stated: a model at recall .95, false-flag .6 passes about .70 against B1 at .5, .2, buying detection with false flags. That is tolerable for a pilot go only; D-S33's false-positive rule still binds B3, and false flags are printed beside the verdict. (3, 4) The binomial assumed independent claims and failed real discrimination: replaced by the stratified test, which cost power (at recall .5, false-flag .1, .981 to .935, and .735 at table correlation .4) and held every table-level no-skill case at or below .021. (5) B1's abstentions and truncations are printed in each row, and the void rule added. (6) Free parameters removed: `--leave-out` is gone, the items come from the digest above, `bar_refusal` gives a run of any other items no verdict, and `g1_scores.json` records both digests. The first score of the one pass stands. (7) D-235's six discordant documents size the later paired test and are not a G1 condition; counts in each direction are printed per benchmark, by document. (8) Relevance is now gated on ContraDoc through the key's evidence units (condition 4); SciTab has none, so a whole cell is accepted there and the lead reads every listed quote before saying go; a run whose flags quote nothing relevant is reported as such. (9) The floor of 2 is inert beside condition 3 (at no false flag it needs about 5 on ContraDoc): "two correct flags pass" is false. (10) Scope of the false-pass figure: .0026 is for no skill on both benchmarks; no skill on ContraDoc with real skill on SciTab is about .029 a model, .057 for two. (11) This entry and step 2 of the plan bring the records in step, and `passes` is no longer listed among missed conditions. (12) G1's allowance is 256 and B1's 2,048; a truncated G1 reply is refused, so truncations are printed per arm. (13) A stopped pass leaves replies readable before any measurement: such a pass is re-run unchanged and this bar is not amended.
- **Check 321.** 15 proofs, each neutralise, fail, restore, pass.
- **Moves.** G1's launch, until the operator answers A or B: #177.
- **Rules.** D-202, D-235, D-238, D-S22, D-S33, D-S34, III.2 step 3, IV.3, P1, P10.

D-255's conclusion that the variant is not added does not hold for the sample proposed, and is withdrawn.
  3. SERIOUS. The 6-discordant condition passed at .996 or more in every case, silence included, since an abstention counts as wrong, and six against G2 also passed.

The rule itself cites another passage, and 104 of 200 units are under 80 characters, so CLEAR is almost unreachable.

## D-265. Open item 31: an amendment with no REF id came from a document indexed twice

- **When, stage.** 2026-11-06 02:39 +0300, corrected 2026-11-06 03:41 after three checker rounds (system clock, `date`), after v1, step 4, while J1's seal waits on the operator's delete. No launch, no money, no pipeline run. Lane `lane/honesty-2` from `93c2abf`. Issue #39.
- **Diagnosis, from saved runs.** Across the archives of five runs, 193 of 279 amendments carry no REF id: L5v 3 of 6, L7 6 of 6, L8 33 of 45, L12 86 of 120, L12b 65 of 102. All 279 sit at `document-level`, so unit placement worked on none of them. L12b's archives give 102 where its analysis logs sum to 80; no archive repeats another by content, and the difference is not explained. Each no-REF amendment sits on a unit whose heading opens two passages of its own document, because a document under review is indexed as `context` and as `operational` under one id, and `unit_passage_refs` leaves a unit with two hits unplaced; each has exactly one operational passage. The lead counted L5v, L12 and L12b, and the checker confirmed the same for all five. These counts match headings read from each amendment's comment against `reference_index.json`, not a replay of the function. L1, named in the item's evidence, is not under `external/s05` and was not read.
- **Fix.** `paired_review.review_copy` keeps a document's operational rows when it has any. `one_claim` refuses a passage two units claim: the second copy had been refusing that case by accident, for instance a heading repeated past the 200-passage cap. Row units share their table's passage, rightly, and keep it. Two passages under review stay refused, and a grounding copy alone places as before.
- **What moves.** Every amendment on such a document, not only the 193: its location and its comment's citation sentence change from document level to the unit's passage. `cited_refs` keeps a compared passage in `ref_ids` beside the unit's own, which placing would otherwise have dropped, so `cited_by` still agrees with the comment.
- **A false note, found by the checker.** `model_item_notes` told a reader that a model cited something other than its unit's passage when it cited that unit's own text: its other copy, or a paragraph under its heading. The note occurs 103 times across `external/s05`, the deliverables repeating one another. In the five runs `review_findings.md` holds 50; the second checker could tie 26 to a unit with an approximate lookback, 9 of them own text and 17 true, and the other 24 are unread. `PlacedUnits` carries the document's excerpts and `in_own_unit` tests whole paragraphs, reading an excerpt of 200 characters or more by its start because it may be clipped. Another unit's own passage keeps its note. A paragraph repeated word for word in two units can draw no note where one was due; a row unit citing the other copy of its table keeps the false note, since its paragraph is one row, not the table; and an agent record on a document with nothing placed keeps the old note (`unit_refs or {}` in the pinned renderer drops the excerpts).
- **What stays.** A unit past the passage cap, or under a repeated heading, is still unplaced, and its amendment still has no REF id and its validator errors. That is stated, not closed.
- **`agent` stays empty, said in the code.** Empty on all 279: only computed findings become amendments and Python wrote them, so filling the field would name an agent that did not write it (`derived_from` carries the provenance).
- **Scoring.** No rule changed and no saved run is re-scored: `tools/score_corpus.py` matches on unit, relation, rule and text, and the adapters read no `ref_ids`, `source_refs` or `location`. One display moves: `score_corpus.py` prints a `source_refs` count, which rises on new runs.
- **Rules.** D-S23 item 5, D-178, P11, P1, P10.

## D-274. P2 (a)'s first attack: what the design can reach, and its bar before any reply

- **When, stage.** 2026-11-06 17:42 +0300 (system clock, `date`), after v1, P2 (a), beside J1. No pair reply exists. Lane `lane/find-judge` at `7a475b0`, with `lane/judge-1` merged into it because the replay needs J1's named candidate; that merge is the lane's, and the loop branch does not take it until the lane is merged.
- **Attack, round 1 (fresh checker): 2 CRITICAL, 7 SERIOUS, 4 MINOR.** No key read by the checker.
- **CRITICAL 1, answered.** The lead's "27 of 30 with limit 40" counted any pair touching the marked sentence. The checker measured, with no key, that an arbitrary sentence would touch 24.8 of 30 at that limit, so the count said almost nothing, and the limit was fixed on it. It is withdrawn as a reach figure. The key keeps no text of the sentence the evidence contradicts, so `score_corpus.marked_passages` now reads it from the benchmark's own source through the adapter. Two more looks at gold were taken for this, counts only, on these same 60 documents, and they chose the ranker: the ranker and the limit are fitted here, and no reach figure below is a measurement.
- **What the design can reach, counts only, of the 30 gold documents.** 4 name no partner in the source. 1 names one that matches no passage. 7 have both marks on one passage, which a pair cannot hold; the source's own `scope` field reads intra on 7, local on 14, global on 9. 18 have two separate marked passages, and of these a top-40 pair holds both on 12 by word overlap, 14 by bge-m3, 15 by both together. **Chosen: bge-m3 alone, 40 pairs,** the same calls as words, and the ranker the plan named. A flag can therefore stand on the partner in at most 14 documents, and a contradiction inside one sentence is out of this step's reach, stated.
- **SERIOUS 7, answered: no benchmark artefact in the proposer.** The top pair's word score against gold, AUC 0.48. It is also carried into `read` as a Python-only control.
- **CRITICAL 2, answered.** `read` now refuses a pass that is not complete, other prompts, keys, source or comparator (each by digest, in the bar file), and a folder already holding a result. Check 324 holds a whole read on an invented pass with those refusals, 12 proofs. The comparator is named: both J1 groups' B1 on the 60 documents, the higher net, void past D-241's abstain floor.
- **The bar, `both_orders`, written before any reply.** Calls readable at least 95 percent. Flagged documents at most 80 percent. By document, counted as B1 is: net above the same model's B1, precision at least B1's when B1 has at least 5 flags, net above the Python control at the same number of flags, chance tail at most 0.05. By place: at least 5 gold documents with a flag on the partner or, where no separate partner exists, touching the mark, and those at least half of the gold documents flagged. Result `keep`, `not_kept` or `void`.
- **Why these.** 0.05 and not J1's 0.0125: J1's was 0.05 over four looks, and this is one variant on one benchmark. Net "above B1" here is a gate for one harness step, not D-S33's "above", which needs the paired interval on the larger sample: `keep` meets no target, says the record, and the report gives both tails. The place test is kept apart from the document count because B1 has none, which was the unfairness in SERIOUS 5.
- **SERIOUS 3 and 4, reported rather than controlled.** Both orders is an unmeasured control, and greedy decoding keeps a content error across orders. `read` reports the contradict rate on clear documents, order agreement, flagged pairs per document, pairs on the mark, cannot-tell calls and replies run to the allowance. No pilot: the pass is cheap, and the bar reads the whole of it.
- **SERIOUS 8 and 9, fixed.** Identity is read on every word, so "shall not" against "shall" and 5 days against 9 days stay pairs. A sentence is marked on its best passage alone, by overlap. MINOR 10: a short stretch closing a line joins the sentence before it.
- **Left, stated.** The early stop sees only the first 12 prompts. The analyser will describe the pass as document-level judging. The embedding ranker differs by device, so prompts are built once, here, and the product's ranking is not byte for byte the measured one. Shared labels and figures are not built, so `not_kept` says nothing of them. Redact-and-retry is not built. `Judge only from the two passages` hides pronouns and time. A true contradiction in a clear document counts as false. Replies' reasons are not read: right for the right reason is not shown, and P2 (c) is not here.
- **Prompts.** `external/s05/P2A/p2a_prompts.json`, 4,800 prompts, `07e10bf7fa57...`. The bar file follows J1's read, whose digest it names.
- **Rules.** III.2 step 3, IV.4, D-S26, D-S30, D-S33, D-S38, D-S39, P1, P10.

SciTab, 35 items: `judge_direct` 14 right, 17 false, 89 percent flagged, chance .938, readable under 95 percent; `judge_reason` 13 right, 10 false, net +3 above C1, chance .239, precision under B1's. - **What the same model did bare (B1, the same run), and why it matters more than the verdict.** With reasoning, as shipped: **SciTab 93 items, macro-F1 .838, accuracy .806, 35 right, 4 false; ContraDoc 60 items, accuracy .567, 6 right, 2 false.** Direct: SciTab macro-F1 .711, 5 abstained; ContraDoc accuracy .550, 6 right, 3 false. - **When, stage.** 2026-11-08 19:38 +0300 (system clock, `date`), after v1, D-315, III.2 step 3, IV.4 round 1.
- **Checker** `bar-check` (fresh, read-only) on `lane/choice-2` `763b1881` and the calibration on `lane/train` `e4e048ee`: 13 gaps. Two break guarantees the bar claims: the calibration's fresh-document check compares source ids with staged ids and can never fire (`fresh_test.py:184-186`; half B is not refused either, against D-S62 item 5), and the read-once key is file bytes, so re-spacing a file or refitting the calibration allows a second read (`fresh_test.py:255-257`). The others: the reads file can be deleted (3); a crash after scoring leaves labels with no read counted (4); nothing ties the calibration to its half A fit (5); C_BAR's net, placed and per-document void rules dropped without a record (7); B1 readability pooled across groups (8); no attempt number in the result (9); only the user text proven byte for byte the pipeline's call (10); the training overlap filter may not cover the 38 moved documents (11); 9 moved siblings of fresh documents staged but unexcluded (12); one document per group enforced upstream only (13). The 38 built with `--side holdout` are byte-identical to `build_moved` and change nothing (its Q7).
- **Every gap is closed in code before the read, not in prose,** except where named here: `choice-build` closes 1 (both sides mapped to source ids through the items files, half B refused, the proof on the real calibrator's output), 2 (key on document ids, key content, the trained group's prompt ids and `user_sha256`, the calibration out of the key and one calibration per adapter; a re-spaced file refused), 3 (the read refuses to run once a committed marker names the set; the reads file's digest goes in DECISIONS after the read), 4 (the read counted before the scorer opens any key), 5 (the read refits the calibration from the half A rows in the same prompts file with `judge_calibration.calibrate` and refuses unequal values), 7 (C_BAR items 1, 5 and the per-document void added to the verdict), 8 (readability void per B1 group; the comparator rule is fixed in code before the read and picks on fresh data, stated here), 9 (attempt number and the earlier attempts' outcomes in the result: attempt 1 was C base, T and half B, D-291 to D-294), 10 (a proof on the full rendered input, system text and chat template, against `AgentWrapper.call_choice` on a fixture), 13 (one document per group checked in the bar against the groups file and `parts.json`, with a neutralised proof). `train-judge` closes 11 (the overlap counter run over the built rows against `ContraDoc.moved.json`'s text, no labels, 0 hits required, else rebuild) and the calibration side of 1 and 5.
- **The 9 siblings (12)** in `external/s05/D-S56/build_moved/` that are not in the fresh set are never read, trained or calibrated on, and are added to every overlap filter and to the ontology lane's sources.

No more licensed fresh material exists (D-297, D-S63), so the test runs at 100 documents, the most there is. Before the read, `choice-build` writes into the result the power at the trained judge's own half A effect (from the calibration's half A figures) with its interval, beside the .80. A pass is reported as a pass; a failure is reported as "not shown at this size", never as "no effect", with both power figures stated.
- **The test is of the judge alone** (one narrow question on Python-selected pairs), not of the full system; every report says so (D-S62 item 1 asks for the full system: that stays the step 5 cases and the sealed run).
- **Rules.** III.2 step 3, IV.4, D-S45 item 7, D-S46 item 1, D-S56 item 4, D-S62 items 1 and 5, C_BAR, P8.

## D-319. Round 3 of the position comparison: compare only quotes that differ in their figure alone

- **When, stage.** 2026-11-08 20:02 +0300 (system clock, `date`), after v1, IV.4 round 3 (the last) on `lane/cases-1` `e54b04a5`.
- **Round 3** (`movement-check`): every earlier attack refuses with a true reason; position and gap records agree on every figure and unit. Open: five new quote shapes still give confident wrong records (the period in the subject, "The monthly rent is 9,000 EUR." against "The yearly rent is 108,000 EUR."; after a comma, a dash or a full stop; before the figure without a comma; words compared as sets, not places) (3 to 7, SERIOUS: a reader is misled); two refusal names claim more than is true (`measure_longer_than_read` for a three-word measure followed by a verb; `measure_in_brackets` for a bracket holding no measure) (8, 9); the docstring "a position carries no figure the gap would refuse" is false, and a position record carries the same wrong unit (13, 14). The worked case computes no movement (0 of 16 rows; seven refused `words_after_measure`, not five).
- **Cause.** Every rule so far reads a window around the figure; any word outside the window can change the measure, so no window rule can make a computed movement safe, and deciding what an outside word means is a WORDS-A decision.
- **Fix (the structural rule that is safe by construction).** Python computes a gap between two quotes only when they are identical, as written (whitespace collapsed, case kept), except for the one figure each holds: "Notice: 90 days" against "Notice: 30 days", "The lease runs for 10 years." against "The lease runs for 5 years." Every other pair is refused `quotes_differ_outside_figure`. The earlier window rules are then not needed for safety and their reasons go (8 and 9 fall away); a position record carries a value and unit only when it takes part in a computed gap, otherwise its figure is left out with that reason, and the docstring says exactly that (13, 14). attack.py and attack2.py's quotes become neutralised proofs; the worked case's measured score is whatever the rule gives, each refusal named. A computed movement then means "the same sentence with only the figure changed", stated in POSITION-GAPS-A and on every case result.
- **Then** one fresh tie-break checker (IV.4) on the fix, with this record and the attacks; if it confirms nothing open, the lane joins step 5. Open item 93 stays (a declared unit per issue is what would let more pairs compute).
- **Rules.** IV.4, WORDS-A, P8, D-S58, D-317.
