## D-330. The success rules attacked: 14 gaps and one rule for all lanes; the target table

- **When, stage.** 2026-11-08 21:19 +0300 (system clock, `date`), after v1, D-324 to D-326, D-S72, D-S73.
- **`success-check`** (fresh) on the four rules (judge `e531b30b`, auditor `f5ef3ad7`, ontology `415385ad`, producer `d56c1c56`): 4 CRITICAL, 6 SERIOUS, 4 MINOR, plus 4 on the producer's new sections. As written, no rule guarantees what D-S72 item 2 asks.
- **One rule for every lane (the CRITICAL multiplicity, item 2).** Attempts run until success (D-S72), so each held-out opening spends error: the k-th opening of a part's held-out material is tested at alpha 0.05 / 2^k (one-sided), so the chance of any false success over every attempt of that part stays at most 0.05. Every opening is counted in a tracked ledger, `docs/loop/HELDOUT_OPENINGS.md`, written by the lead before the result is read; a lane's code refuses to score its held-out part unless that ledger's line for the attempt exists and is committed, and a committed record shows the candidate passed its tuning part, each with a neutralised proof (item 6). The held-out part tells the next recipe pass or fail only, never which items (L-4).
- **The judge (items 1, 3, 4, 5, 14).** Half B is spent: it was read for T and its figures shaped 2e's recipe (`TRAIN_JUDGE_DATA.md:226`), so it cannot be the held-out part; line 335's claim is corrected. `train-judge` counts, by ids only and with no key opened, the ContraDoc and SciTab development items no read, bar, recipe or lesson has touched (the fresh set and its 9 siblings excluded). If such items exist they become the held-out reserve; if not, the rule says the judge's success is shown on its tuning half only, labelled in-sample, and its confirmation is the system's fresh read. The held-out test is a sign test at the spent alpha, with the benchmark named in advance (SciTab, since ContraDoc's reach caps any gain). The trained judge's SciTab threshold is fixed in code before the seal by the same rule as the base's, both forms tempered the same way; the base is re-run in the 2e session or proved byte-identical to C base. B1's figures and the D-S73 bar stand beside every result.
- **The producer (items 8, 9, 6 and 8.4).** The split is keyed on the document, not the call (or a committed count shows no document on both sides). The margins are restated as the smallest net counts that pass the stated test. The held-out pass is built with the refusal above before attempt 1 launches. 8.4b says what is measured ("k of 26 valid without the constraint"), not a guard it is not; "would remove, once INFRA-050 lands and is measured"; one role count, and bundle 1 named by digest.
- **The auditor (items 10, 11, 12).** The held-out half shares ContractNLI's 17 rules and near-duplicate boilerplate: the rule states that limit beside any success, or the held-out half is also split by rule. Criterion 3 is defined when the untrained form has no usable threshold; criterion 4's second opening is counted; half B gives pass or fail only. A short search record backs "no published counterpart".
- **The ontology (items 7, 13).** Its margin was written at 20:58 after attempt 1 launched at 20:30, so attempt 1 is outside the rule (reported as a measurement, not a success), and the rule starts at attempt 2, with the margin as a constant in code and a proof; an explicit block table (the formula gave the training block); the earlier best measured on each new block; a power line and the synthetic-only limit.
- **The target table** (`target-table`, papers and leaderboards only, each figure read at its source): SciTab's bar is 65 macro-F1 on three classes (MACE, a 2026 preprint, 0.65, beside GPT-4 zero-shot 64.80 in the SciTab paper's Table 4; close, not exact: MACE pairs an 8B planner and executor with a 20B verifier); ContraDoc's bar is 0.681 document-level accuracy (LLaMA3.2-90B, one judge-and-quote prompt on all 891 documents, Tan et al. 2026; close, not exact: one prompt, not an agentic system, and Shimmer scores development subsets with their counts and intervals). Two starting points were corrected: ContraDoc's GPT-4o 0.68 is from Tan et al., not the benchmark paper, and GPT-4's 78 on SciTab is the two-class setting. Peer-reviewed open small-model SciTab points sit near 45. B1 on SciTab (J1, .838 on 93 development claims) already stands above the published bar. `table-check` attacks the table before any bar uses it.

## D-376. The primary metric per benchmark, from its own paper (D-S99, vekil metric-check)

9 November 2026, 17:00 +0300, lead session ac63cd67.

`metric-check` (Opus, fresh) read each paper's PDF and our code (loop/2026-10-27; the three newer adapters on lane/causal e0039457).
- **SciTab** (Lu et al., EMNLP 2023, Table 4 p.7): macro-F1 in 2-class and 3-class settings. Ours is 3-class, since "cannot be settled" is a real third class (scitab/adapter.py:57-60). The gate reads SciTab in 3-class macro-F1 over the fixed three classes. judge_read.macro_f1 (judge_read.py:150-155), which averages over the gold classes present, is fixed to use all three, with a proof. The bootstrap is over tables, a stated departure from "over items". G1/J1's bar is labelled a refutes-flag test, never macro-F1.
- **ContraDoc** (Li et al., NAACL 2024, Table 2 p.7): binary judgment accuracy, with P, R and F1. Ours matches (contradoc/adapter.py:229-266). "evidence_containment" is the paper's R-acc(pos), not EHR, and is renamed; EHR is added over true positives; our exact containment is stated as stricter than BERTScore > .98; B3's figure is labelled "unit-level, not the paper's EHR".
- **PUBHEALTH** (Kotonya and Toni, EMNLP 2020, Table 4 p.7): 4-class macro-F1. B3 can answer only three ways, so B1 and the cloud reference get a 4-class entry; B3's 3-class figure is labelled "mapped, not the paper's setting"; figures are reweighted to the test mix.
- **CLadder** (Jin et al., NeurIPS 2023, Table 2 p.8): accuracy. It is labelled "close" (v1 balanced file, not v1.0 aggregate) and reweighted to the rung mix.
- **Corr2Cause** (Jin et al., ICLR 2024, Table 4 p.7): F1 of the valid class. The probe's primary test becomes a paired bootstrap on F1, with McNemar as a labelled secondary; role B confirms the test version.
- **Earlier figures restated.** D-365's SciTab ".822 and .800" were accuracy. In macro-F1 (cloud_reference_score.json) they are reference B1 .891 direct and .888 reasoning, local .734 and .918, on 45 claims, recomputed after the fixed-classes fix. The judging-step macro-F1 values, over 14 items with the classes present, are recomputed. D-371's "10 points above B1's accuracy" reads, for SciTab, 3-class macro-F1. D-277, C_BAR, D-366 to D-370, L-10 and L-11 are marked "3-class, classes present" until a subset without NEI gold is ruled out. Any ContraDoc evidence figure is relabelled R-acc(pos). TARGET_TABLE.md agrees with the papers.
- **Owners:** `choice-build` (the gate's scoring, the judge_read fix, the ContraDoc renames and EHR); `other-domains` and `causal-probe` (PUBHEALTH, CLadder, Corr2Cause, after the gate); `demo-console` (the dashboard's metric labels).

## D-380. SciTab's class setting declared per item set; the gate draws not-enough-info claims (D-S99)

9 November 2026, 17:03 +0300, lead session ac63cd67.

- **The rule:** the class setting is declared per item set, 2-class when it holds no NEI gold and 3-class otherwise. Macro-F1 averages over that setting's gold classes, and an NEI prediction on a 2-class item counts as a miss for its gold class. scitab/adapter.py's headline, judge_read.macro_f1 and the gate scoring take the declared setting, never reading it off the gold present (`choice-build`, with proofs both ways).

Every comparison of these with 0.65 or 64.80, both 3-class, is not like for like. D-370's "below B1 .838" stands, since both are 2-class. Our 2-class setting is "close", not the same, since the paper excludes NEI items while we count an NEI answer as wrong.

## D-505. One method for every fine-tuning (Seckin, 00:09)

12 November 2026, lead session b547ef8e. Seckin, 00:09: a standing rule for all fine-tuning (the judge, the auditor, any later model). Standing order 71. It starts after 12 November 11:00, with the held lanes (D-503), not tonight.

1. Before use, check that the training data is balanced (label shares, source shares, no single source dominant) and that it shares nothing with any test or held-out set. The overlap is proven with the leakage tool (GATE-LEAKAGE-A), not asserted.
2. Split the data into parts and train on the first part.
3. Measure on development items the model never trained on.
4. Analyse the errors by kind.
5. Build an edge-case stress set from those error kinds and test against it separately.
6. Choose the next training part from the kinds where the model is weak.
7. Repeat until the development score stops rising. Only then go to any gate or sealed test. Gate and sealed items never choose or tune anything.
After 11:00, a lane on Sonnet reads the records (the judge's attempts, L-11 and D-370; the producer's, L-12, PRODUCER_TRAINING_PLAN and D-330; the auditor's) and lists which of the seven steps each training already did and which are missing. The missing steps are adopted in the next training round without asking him. The audit's result goes to FOR_SECKIN.
- **Rules.** D-503, GATE-LEAKAGE-A, D-330, D-422, Seckin 00:09.

## D-506. Three additions to D-505: a working and a held-back half; every tuning step; a power analysis (Seckin, 00:15)

12 November 2026, lead session b547ef8e. Seckin, 00:15. These widen D-505 and start with it, after 12 November 11:00. Standing order 71 is widened.

1. The development items are split in two. The working part is used every round for error analysis and choices. The held-back part is opened only now and then, to measure, and each opening is counted (as HELDOUT_OPENINGS and choice_read's read-b count do). If the working part rises and the held-back part does not, that is fitting to the working part, not progress.
2. The rule covers every tuning step, not only fine-tuning. How the question is asked, how evidence is chosen, thresholds and calibration all follow the same loop and the same split. Gate and sealed items never enter any choice.
3. A power analysis. Is each half large enough to detect the differences that matter: the gate's 10-point bar (a) and 5-point bar (b) margins, and the gains from one round to the next? The existing simulators (tools/negotiation_power.py, gate_score's bootstrap) are the basis. If a half is too small, the development set is enlarged from benchmark material that is not reserved for the gate or the sealed tests, under the overlap rules (GATE-LEAKAGE-A). The training set itself does not need to grow for this.
- **Rules.** D-505, D-330, D-422, GATE-LEAKAGE-A, Seckin 00:15.

## D-531. A blank cheque for speed-ups that cost no accuracy (Seckin, 14:36)

12 November 2026, 14:40 +0300, lead session b547ef8e. Seckin, 14:36, a standing order (order 73): any method that shortens time without costing accuracy may be used, for example batching PRACTICE_AUDITOR's independent (unit, rule) calls on the GPU, splitting work across several Lambda machines, or running independent parts side by side. The lead does not wait for him to raise each one. Every stage looks for such speed-ups, and the development plan is adapted to them. The method:
1. A small test, not a large one, shows that outputs or accuracy are unchanged.
2. If so, the method is adopted where it is most effective. If not, the slower way stays and the reason is recorded.
3. Extra cost is fine unless it is a cliff, within the existing caps.
4. Nothing under the sealed 14 November measurement changes in the middle of it. A speed-up proven output-identical may go in before the seal; anything else comes after the read.
TIME_BUDGET.md's causes are the first candidates: the auditor's sequential calls and the long single generations. AFTER_V1_PLAN gains a section listing them, with the small test each needs. The first test (a: batched judging replies against one-by-one, byte for byte, through the replay pass on Lambda) is scheduled once the gate set is drawn, because it must not disturb role B or the gate run.

## D-538. Each model's weight on the weekly limit, from our own data; the gate-prep lane ran on Fable until 13:41 today

12 November 2026, 17:30 +0300, lead session b547ef8e. Seckin, 17:18: estimate each model's weight on the weekly limit from our own data only.
- **Readings used.** 12 seven-day readings from 11 November 11:22 (1 percent) to 12 November 16:36 (74 percent), taken from the records: 11:22 1, 12:12 4, 12:51 7, 13:18 9, 14:34 12, 19:33 24, 00:03 34, 02:04 38, 05:01 46, 08:04 52, 13:43 68, 16:36 74. That gives 11 windows.
- **Tokens.** Per window, the tokens of every assistant record in the Claude Code session logs, by model and type, deduplicated.
- **Fit.** Non-negative least squares, with a bootstrap over windows for 90 percent intervals.
  - Fit A uses per model the tokens other than cache reads, plus one pooled cache-read term: Opus 1.08 percent per million (0 to 2.78), Fable 0.89 (0 to 1.07), Sonnet 0.00 (0 to 2.15), cache reads 0.012 (0 to 0.038). Residual sd 2.0 points.
  - Fit B, per model output and cache write, is too thin to read. Fable output comes out at 21.5 percent per million (0.5 to 33), and the other terms have intervals from 0 to more than 17.
- **Limits.** 11 windows; the models overlap in most windows; Sonnet appears in only 5 windows; claude.ai and other non-Claude-Code use is not in the logs, but it is in the readings. The figures are a rough weight, not a price.
- **Found, a departure by the lead.** The gate-prep lane was started on Fable on 11 November. D-479 (13:17) said running Fable lanes finish their current step and stop, with later work on Opus. The lead kept giving gate-prep new tasks instead (the fingerprint restarts, the audit scan, the listed-rows mode), so it ran on Fable until 12 November 13:41: 56.8 M tokens other than cache reads after 13:17 on 11 November. That is most of the Fable share and of the Fable 81 percent reading. The lane was stopped at 13:45 today; no transcript shows Fable after 13:41. From now on a lane's model is checked before the lead gives it a new task.

## D-540. Binding usage rules for every lead session (Seckin, 17:40)

12 November 2026, 17:55 +0300, lead session b547ef8e. Seckin, 17:40: standing usage rules that are never deviated from (order 75). They are written into LOOP_STATE so that every handoff carries them.
1. **Lead context stays small.** When the lead passes 30 to 40 percent context, it writes the handoff and a fresh session takes over. While waiting on a job, it wakes at the job's estimated end, not by frequent polling, so that an expired cache does not rewrite the whole context each time. Departure, stated: this session is at about 90 percent now. It writes the handoff at this point and asks Seckin to start a fresh lead.
2. **Model and effort by task.**
   - The lead runs on Opus, medium effort.
   - Code-writing and checking lanes run on Opus, medium.
   - Only hard work that Opus at medium cannot do runs on Opus, high (the old Fable work).
   - Records, the README, file reading and summaries run on Sonnet.
   - Counting, summing, searching and other mechanical work is done by script, with no model.
   - Fable is never used.
3. **Review rounds are sized to the change:** one independent round for a small fix; three rounds and a tie-break only for large or risky changes.
4. **Usage by model** is counted from the session logs at every FOR_SECKIN report (tools/loop/model_use_check.py), together with the D-539 lane-model line. The per-model weight fit of D-538 is redone on 19 November, after a week of data.
Any deviation from these rules is reported in FOR_SECKIN at once, with its reason.
- **Rules.** D-479, D-503, D-537, D-538, D-539, Seckin 17:40.
